body:
## Overview

Introduce a lightweight **Onboarding Tour** to guide new users through the core features of Cocktail Chooser.

The app currently contains powerful features (filters, logging, persistent selection), but they are not immediately discoverable.

This tour will:

- Highlight key UI areas
- Guide users through the intended workflow
- Reduce confusion on first use

The tour should be:

- Short (4 steps)
- Focused on actions, not explanations
- Automatically shown on first launch (once per version)
- Re-runnable from the menu

---

# Goals

1. Help users quickly understand how to use the app
2. Improve discoverability of logging and filters
3. Establish the “your bar” mental model
4. Reduce friction in first-time usage

---

# Tour Flow (4 Steps)

## Step 1 — Menu (Account + Bar)

Highlight: Main menu

Text:

Start here. Create an account and add your ingredients so we can show you what you can make.

---

## Step 2 — Filters (Core Functionality)

Highlight:

- Only Cocktails I Can Make
- Popular Only
- Show Untried Only

Text:

Use filters to narrow down your options.  
Try “Only Cocktails I Can Make” to see drinks you can make right now.

Tip: “Untried Only” works best once you start logging drinks.

---

## Step 3 — Filter Button (Advanced Filtering)

Highlight: Filter button

Text:

Tap here for advanced filtering like occasion, season, and more.

---

## Step 4 — Selected Cocktail + Logging Panel (Bottom Section)

Behavior:

- Automatically select a default cocktail (e.g. Old Fashioned)
- Scroll the user to the bottom panel
- Highlight the selected cocktail section

Text:

When you select a cocktail, it stays here.  
This is where you can log, rate, and revisit it.

---

# Implementation Approach

## Use Library (Recommended)

Use a lightweight onboarding/tour library:

Options:

- Shepherd.js
- Intro.js
- Driver.js (preferred for simplicity)

Requirements:

- Highlight DOM elements
- Dim background
- Tooltip positioning
- Next / Previous navigation
- Auto-scroll to elements

---

## Tour Behavior

- Launch automatically on first app load (after feature release)
- Can be dismissed at any time
- Can be restarted from menu (e.g. “Help” or “Show Tutorial”)

---

## State Management

Use localStorage:

Example:

onboarding_v1_completed = true

Future updates can increment version:

onboarding_v2_completed

---

## Technical Notes

- Ensure tour works on both mobile and desktop
- Ensure proper z-index layering above modals and UI
- Handle elements that may not yet be visible (scroll into view)
- Step 4 requires programmatic selection of a cocktail

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- Tour runs automatically for first-time users
- Tour contains exactly 4 steps
- Each step highlights the correct UI element
- Step 4 scrolls to and highlights the selected cocktail panel
- Tour can be dismissed at any time
- Tour can be re-triggered from the menu
- Tour works on mobile and desktop
- Tour does not interfere with normal app usage after completion

---

# Notes

This feature focuses on **guiding user behavior**, not explaining the system.

Each step should clearly answer:

“What should I do next?”
title: Introduce a lightweight **Onboarding Tour** to guide new users through the core features of Cocktail Chooser.

body:
## Overview

When a user selects a cocktail from the list, the cocktail detail modal opens correctly and supports viewing and printing.

However, after the modal is closed, users may not realize that:

- the selected cocktail remains open below the cocktail list
- the selected cocktail panel is where drink logging happens
- logging is necessary to make Tried / Untried filters meaningful

This creates a usability problem where an important feature exists but is not discoverable.

---

# Goals

1. Make it obvious that a cocktail remains selected after the modal is closed
2. Make drink logging easy to discover
3. Guide users from viewing a cocktail to logging it

---

# Problem

Current behavior:

- User opens cocktail from the list
- User closes modal
- User sees cocktail list again
- User may assume the interaction is complete

Missing affordance:

- No clear indication that the selected cocktail is still available below the list
- No obvious call-to-action to log the drink

As a result, users may never use drink logging, making the Tried / Untried features much less valuable.

---

# Proposed UX

After the cocktail detail modal is closed, show a visible selected-cocktail action row near the top of the main list area.

Example:

Selected: Negroni

[ Log Cocktail ]

Optional future secondary action:

[ View Selected Cocktail ]

The primary action should scroll the user to the selected cocktail panel where the logging controls already exist.

---

# Functional Requirements

## Selected Cocktail Indicator

Display the name of the currently selected cocktail after the modal closes.

Example:

Selected: Old Fashioned

## Primary CTA

Show a prominent button:

Log Cocktail

Behavior:
- Scroll to the selected cocktail panel below the list
- Bring logging controls into view

## Persistence

The selected cocktail indicator should remain visible while a cocktail is selected.

It should update when a different cocktail is selected.

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- After closing a cocktail modal, the UI clearly indicates which cocktail is currently selected
- A visible `Log Cocktail` button is shown
- Clicking the button scrolls the user to the selected cocktail panel
- The workflow from view → log is clear on mobile and desktop
- Existing logging functionality remains unchanged

---

# Notes

This issue is primarily about discoverability and usability, not about changing the logging model itself.

The goal is to surface an already-existing feature so users understand how to use it.
title: Improve Cocktail Logging discoverability / UX affordance

body:
# Overview

Users frequently lack one ingredient required for a cocktail.

Example:

Negroni requires:

Gin  
Sweet Vermouth  
Campari

User has:

Gin  
Sweet Vermouth  
❌ Campari

However they *do* have:

Aperol

Which is a reasonable substitute.

A **Substitution Engine** would allow the app to suggest:

"Makeable with substitution"

or

"Try this variation"

This improves usability and encourages experimentation.

---

# Goals

Allow the app to:

1. Suggest ingredient substitutions
2. Mark cocktails as **Makeable with Substitution**
3. Recommend acceptable alternatives when ingredients are missing

---

# Example UX

Cocktail Card:

Negroni

Missing: Campari

Suggested substitution:
Aperol

You can make this variation.

---

# Functional Requirements

## Substitution Mapping

Create a substitution table:

Substitutions

Columns:

Id  
IngredientId  
SubstituteIngredientId  
ConfidenceScore (optional)  
Notes (optional)

Example rows:

Campari → Aperol  
Cointreau → Triple Sec  
Lemon Juice → Lime Juice  

---

## Matching Logic

Current engine:

```
canMake = all ingredients present
```

New logic:

```
canMake = all ingredients present
OR
canMakeWithSubstitution = missing ingredients have valid substitutions
```

---

## Cocktail Evaluation Metadata

Extend evaluation result:

```
{
  cocktailId,
  canMake,
  missingIngredients,
  substitutionsAvailable
}
```

---

# UI Behavior

When substitution is possible:

Show badge:

```
Makeable with Substitution
```

Detail view shows:

```
Substitute Aperol for Campari
```

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- Substitution table created
- Matching engine checks substitutions
- Cocktails display substitution suggestions
- Substitution does not modify original recipe
- Feature can be disabled if desired

---

# Future Enhancements

## Substitution Confidence

Score substitutions:

High
Medium
Experimental

---

## Flavor Graph

Eventually build an ingredient similarity network.

---

## User Custom Substitutions

Allow users to define:

"My substitute for Campari"

---
title: Ingredient Substitution Engine

When an idea is selected for development, create a GitHub issue and link it here.

# Discovery & Recommendation

## Ingredient Substitution Engine
Allow users to substitute ingredients they do not have with similar ingredients.

Examples:

Campari → Aperol  
Cointreau → Triple Sec  
Lemon Juice → Lime Juice (sometimes)

This would allow cocktails to appear as:

"Makeable with Substitution"

or

"Try This Variation"

Potential impact:
- increases cocktail discovery
- reduces friction when users are missing ingredients

This idea should become a **formal issue**.

```

## Garnish Intelligence

Show garnish substitutions.

Hide cocktails requiring garnishes I don't have
```

## Cocktail History Expansion

Optional expandable panel:

- historical notes

You already store some of this.

## Bar Completeness Score

Example:

Bar completeness: **17%**

Gamifies bar building.

---

## Social / Sharing (Future)

Allow users to share:

"My Bar"

Example link:

cocktailchooser.com/bar/seth

Friends can see what you can make.

---

# Admin / Data Quality

## Ingredient Alias Mapping

Example:

```
Fresh Lime Juice
Lime Juice
Lime
```

Canonical:

```
Lime Juice
```

Prevents duplicates.

---

## Recipe Variant Detection

Example:

Two Negroni recipes:

- Book A
- Book B

Allow grouping of variants.

Related to Issue #39.

---

# Long-Term Vision Ideas

## Flavor Recommendation Engine

Example:

User likes:

Negroni  
Boulevardier  

Suggest:

Old Pal

Uses shared ingredients or flavor tags.

---

## AI Cocktail Generator

Input:

"I want something citrusy with bourbon"

Generate:

New cocktail or suggested recipe.

body:
## Overview

Ingredient names currently have **inconsistent casing** in the database.

Examples observed:

- `Gin`
- `gin`
- `Lime Juice`
- `lime juice`
- `Simple Syrup`
- `simple syrup`

This creates several problems:

- Duplicate-looking ingredients
- Poor visual consistency in the UI
- Increased risk of duplicate ingredients during imports
- Harder canonicalization later

This issue standardizes ingredient casing and ensures **future imports are normalized automatically**.

---

# Goals

1. Normalize all existing ingredient names in the database.
2. Enforce a consistent casing rule going forward.
3. Ensure **imported JSON ingredients are automatically normalized**.

---

# Casing Standard

Adopt **Title Case** for ingredient names.

Examples:

| Current | Normalized |
|-------|-------------|
| gin | Gin |
| lime juice | Lime Juice |
| simple syrup | Simple Syrup |
| orange bitters | Orange Bitters |

Rules:

- First letter of each word capitalized
- Trim whitespace
- `NormalizedName` column remains lowercase for comparisons

---

# Database Migration

Since the database already contains a `NormalizedName` column, the migration can safely rebuild the display name from that value.

Steps:

1. Read all rows from `Ingredients`
2. Convert `NormalizedName` to Title Case
3. Update the `Name` column

Pseudo-logic:

```
displayName = TitleCase(NormalizedName)
UPDATE Ingredients SET Name = displayName
```

Migration must:

- Be **idempotent**
- Leave `NormalizedName` untouched
- Not introduce duplicates

---

# Import Pipeline Enforcement

The **Import JSON** feature must normalize ingredient names before insertion.

Steps:

1. Trim whitespace
2. Convert to lowercase to create `NormalizedName`
3. Generate `Name` using Title Case
4. Check for existing ingredient using `NormalizedName`
5. Reuse existing ingredient ID if found

Pseudo-logic:

```
normalized = importName.trim().toLowerCase()
displayName = TitleCase(normalized)

ingredient = findIngredientByNormalizedName(normalized)

if not found:
    create ingredient(Name=displayName, NormalizedName=normalized)
```

This guarantees imports cannot introduce casing inconsistencies.

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- Existing ingredient rows are normalized via migration
- Ingredient names display consistently in the UI
- Import pipeline automatically normalizes casing
- Import cannot create casing duplicates
- No breaking changes to existing cocktails

---

# Optional Enhancements (Post-MVP)

Possible future improvements:

- Ingredient **canonicalization layer**
- Ingredient **alias mapping**

Example:

```
Lime Juice
Fresh Lime Juice
Lime
```

These could map to a canonical ingredient later.

---

# Labels

Suggested:

- `P1 - High`
- `Scope: MVP`
- `Type: Refactor`
- `Type: Data`
title: Normalize Ingredient Casing (Migration + Import Sanitization)

body:
## Overview

Introduce a **Build Your Bar** progress panel that helps users
understand how their current ingredient collection translates into
cocktail capability.

This feature turns the cocktail catalog into a **progression
experience**, helping users discover:

-   What they can make now
-   What they are close to unlocking
-   Which ingredient purchase unlocks the most cocktails

The goal is to create a **reward loop**:

Add ingredient → unlock cocktails → try drinks → repeat.

This dramatically increases user engagement while remaining genuinely
useful.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# MVP Goals

Add a **Build Your Bar** panel that displays:

-   Cocktails the user can make
-   Cocktails that are **Almost Unlocked** (missing one ingredient)
-   Best next ingredient to buy

This panel should encourage exploration without overwhelming the user.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# UI / UX Requirements

### Placement

The panel should appear near the top of the main screen, ideally above
the cocktail list or near filter controls.

Example layout:

Build Your Bar

You can make: 42 cocktails\
Almost unlocked: 18 cocktails

Best next bottle:\
Campari → unlocks 18 cocktails

Optional:

Top 3 next bottles: 1. Campari → unlocks 18 2. Cointreau → unlocks 15 3.
Green Chartreuse → unlocks 12

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Functional Requirements

### 1) Makeable Cocktail Count

Use the existing ingredient matching engine.

Definition:

canMake === true

Display the total number of cocktails that can currently be made.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 2) Almost Unlocked Count

Use the ingredient evaluation metadata.

Definition:

missingCount === 1

Display the number of cocktails that are exactly one ingredient away.

This integrates directly with the **Almost Unlocked filter** defined in
Issue #54.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3) Best Ingredient to Buy

Determine which missing ingredient unlocks the most cocktails.

Algorithm:

1.  Identify cocktails where missingCount === 1
2.  Count occurrences of each missing ingredient
3.  Sort descending
4.  Recommend the ingredient unlocking the most cocktails

Example output:

Campari unlocks 18 cocktails

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Data Model Dependencies

This feature relies on the ingredient evaluation metadata:

{ cocktail, ingredientIds, canMake, missingCount, missingIngredientIds }

The panel should use the **same evaluated cocktail dataset** used by the
filtering system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Performance Considerations

The unlock calculation should operate on the already-computed
evaluatedCocktails list.

Avoid recomputing ingredient comparisons.

Use a simple aggregation pass over cocktails where:

missingCount === 1

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Acceptance Criteria

-   A **Build Your Bar panel** appears in the UI
-   Displays makeable cocktail count
-   Displays almost-unlocked cocktail count
-   Displays best next ingredient to buy
-   Updates automatically when ingredient selections change
-   Uses the existing ingredient evaluation pipeline

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Future Enhancements

Possible extensions:

### Bar Progress Meter

You can make 42 / 320 cocktails\
Bar completeness: 13%

### Spirit Progress Breakdown

Gin cocktails: 18\
Bourbon cocktails: 14\
Rum cocktails: 11

### Unlock Notifications

When a new ingredient is added:

You unlocked 7 new cocktails!

### Ingredient Roadmap

Next upgrades for your bar:

Campari → +18 cocktails\
Cointreau → +15 cocktails\
Green Chartreuse → +12 cocktails

### Achievement System

Examples:

-   Unlock 25 cocktails
-   Try 10 classics
-   Build a 20-bottle bar

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Labels

Suggested:

-   P2 - Medium
-   Scope: Nice-to-Have
-   Type: Core Feature
-   Type: UX
title: Build Your Bar: Progress Panel + Unlock Stats
